question: to the Commission Kris Van Dijck (ECR) Subject:

In its reply to Written Question P-004500/20251, the Commission indicated that certain decarbonisation investments in ports can be supported under Articles 36 and 36b of the General Block Exemption Regulation (Regulation (EU) No 651/2014 (GBER)), including through the notion of ‘vehicles’. However, in the draft revised GBER (in which the relevant provisions are now reflected in Article 54), the definition of ‘vehicle’ has been further specified across transport sectors, but does not explicitly include mobile terminal equipment. At the same time, support for port superstructures appears to remain limited, except in cases linked to intermodality under the Land and Multimodal Transport Guidelines and Transport Block Exemption Regulation. This raises questions regarding the treatment of clean mobile terminal equipment where the primary objective is decarbonisation. 1.
Why do the Land and Multimodal Transport Guidelines and the Transport Block Exemption Regulation not cover aid granted solely for clean mobile terminal equipment?
Why does the draft revised GBER, in particular Article 54 thereof, define the notion of ‘vehicle’ across transport sectors in detail, but not include mobile terminal equipment?
https://www.europarl.europa.eu/doceo/document/P-10-2025-004500_EN.html.
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (10.7.2026) The answer to the first question is the legal basis for the Land and Multimodal Transport Guidelines and for the Transport Block Exemption Regulation. The legal basis for the Land and Multimodal Transport Guidelines and the Transport Block Exemption Regulation is Article 93 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (‘aid for the coordination of transport’). The concept of ‘coordination of transport’ implies an intervention by public authorities that is aimed at guiding the development of the transport sector in the common interest. By contrast, aid with a primary environmental objective, such as decarbonisation, is assessed under Article 107 (3) (c) of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union. It therefore does not fall within the scope of the Land and Multimodal Transport Guidelines and of the Transport Block Exemption Regulation but is assessed under the Commission’s ‘Guidelines on State aid for climate, environmental protection and energy 2022’, if such aid is not blockexempted under Commission Regulation (EU) No 651/2014. On the second question, the Commission’s review of the General Block Exemption Regulation is ongoing. The outcome of the revision cannot be prejudged at this stage.
